subject: general
question: Sometimes, when there is a lack of oxygen in our muscle cells, the pyruvate by anaerobic respiration is converted into:
solution:
The correct answer is __**lactic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During **anaerobic respiration**, which occurs in the absence of oxygen, **pyruvate** is converted into **lactic acid** in the muscle cells.
 
• This process is known as **lactic acid fermentation** and it allows the cells to continue producing **ATP** (energy) despite the lack of oxygen.
 
• The accumulation of **lactic acid** in the muscles can cause **muscle fatigue and soreness**.
 
• This conversion is facilitated by the enzyme **lactate dehydrogenase**.
 
• In contrast to aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration produces far less **ATP**, but it is crucial during intense exercise or when oxygen levels are low.
 
• Lactic acid fermentation is a temporary solution to meet the energy demands of the muscle cells under strenuous conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acetic acid**__

 __
 
• **Acetic acid** is not a product of anaerobic respiration in muscle cells.
 
• It is a key component of **vinegar** and is produced through the fermentation of ethanol by **acetic acid bacteria**.
 
 
 
• **Ethyl alcohol**__
 __
 
• **Ethyl alcohol** (ethanol) is produced during anaerobic respiration in **yeast cells** and some types of bacteria, not in muscle cells.
 
• This process is known as **alcoholic fermentation**.
 
 
 
• **Methyl alcohol**__
 
 
• **Methyl alcohol** (methanol) is not a product of anaerobic respiration.
 
• It is a toxic alcohol that is used industrially as a solvent, antifreeze, and fuel.
